title: Where Our Letters Came From
thesis: A is an ox head rotated 180 degrees. So are B, M and O pictures, still being read every day.

pipeline.narration: SyncVoice (Gemini native audio, voice Kore) via D:/Projects/Utilities/textToSpeechUsingRateLimitlessTTS
pipeline.music: Lyria RealTime (models/lyria-realtime-exp), 126s bed, sidechain-ducked under the voice
pipeline.render: resvg + 24 worker threads -> libx264, 3683 frames in 32s

musicPrompt: Sparse felt piano and a soft plucked kalimba, unhurried, wide space between notes. Warm upright bass far back, faint dusty room tone. Curious and contemplative, a quiet desert-evening patience. Instrumental only, no vocals, no strong melodic hook that competes with a speaking voice.

qa.method: Whisper transcript of the final mux diffed against the script
qa.result: clean; only Whisper's own numeral normalisation ('three thousand eight hundred' heard as '3,800') remains
defectsFound: s05: the standalone letter 'A.' was spoken as 'Ah'
s07: the word 'House.' was dropped entirely
s09: 'water' was dropped from 'In China, water was drawn as'
s13: the recap list lost 'Water', 'Eye' and the letter 'B', and duplicated 'a house'
qa.fix: Every isolated single letter and short standalone word was given a carrier phrase, and the spoken letter list was removed in favour of letting the screen carry it. Content addressing meant only the 6 changed lines re-synthesised.

youtube.title: The letter A is an ox. Upside down.
youtube.description:
Around 3,800 years ago someone in the Sinai drew an ox head. Two horns, a narrow face. Turn it over and you are looking at the letter A.

This one also covers B (a house), M (water) and O (an eye) — and the strange moment where Chinese and the Sinai, with no contact between them, both drew water the same way.

Not Arbitrary: things that look like meaningless convention, shown to be pictures.

tiktok.caption: The letter A is an ox head. Someone drew it 3,800 years ago and we just turned it upside down.
tiktok.hook: First 3 seconds: the letter A flips over and becomes an ox.
